title: Reproduction, Communication & Capstone
description: Study reproduce versus replicate, write a clear research report, review and respond to critique, and capstone: a controlled reproduction study. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Reproduce versus replicate
lessons.description: Describe the evidence obtained and what independent checks remain.
lessons.conceptOverview: A reproduction often aims to recover results using the original artifacts, while an independent replication tests findings with a separately built setup; terminology varies, so state exactly what was reused.
lessons.whyItMatters: Reports should specify reused artifacts and independent choices.

keyTakeaways: Reports should specify reused artifacts and independent choices.

lessons.title: Write a clear research report
lessons.description: Add the missing comparison details and all planned outcomes.
lessons.conceptOverview: Structure a report around the question, method, comparison, results and limits. Keep claims proportional to evidence and provide enough detail for another researcher to inspect the experiment.
lessons.whyItMatters: Transparent methods are necessary to assess reported results.

lessons.title: Review and respond to critique
lessons.description: Plan a corrected experiment and revise the claim based on its outcome.
lessons.conceptOverview: Treat review comments as claims to evaluate against evidence. Correct errors, clarify ambiguity and distinguish additional experiments from edits that only improve exposition.
lessons.whyItMatters: Substantive methodological flaws require substantive correction.

lessons.title: Capstone: a controlled reproduction study
lessons.description: Deliver a literature note, run manifest, comparison table and limitation statement.
lessons.conceptOverview: Select a bounded published claim, document the setup and run a fair baseline plus one controlled extension. Preserve raw results and report deviations, uncertainty and failures.
lessons.whyItMatters: A credible study reports unresolved discrepancies honestly.
